maria: Quick follow-up to the quant-attn RFC thread — I want to lock down the KV-cache / dequant fusion contract before we start rolling kernels. Two problems we need to decide: 1) memory aliasing rules for KV (can kernels read in-place?), and 2) a small 'kernel hint' API so the scheduler can choose inline-dequant vs copy-on-read. TL;DR: I propose we allow aliasing with strict alignment and lifetime guarantees and expose a hint enum {INLINE_DEQUANT, COPY_DEQUANT, NO_DEQUANT}. Thoughts?

jonah: Agree on an explicit contract. Inline dequant is attractive but dangerous if kernels mutate memory. We should require kernels that claim INLINE_DEQUANT to be declared "read-only" for KV pages and to pass a lightweight validation step at load time. Also: quantify perf delta. My local micro-bench (A100, seq_len=1024, bsz=8):
```
strategy       tokens/s
COPY_DEQUANT   12.1k
INLINE_DEQUANT 22.9k
NO_DEQUANT     11.5k
```
So ~1.9x for inline. :eyes:

kevin: Those numbers jive with my runs. Implementation notes: if we allow KV aliasing we must fix the allocator alignment and pin pages to avoid CPU-side remapping during GC. Proposed alias rules: 1) 64-byte alignment, 2) no reallocation of aliasable pages for the lifetime of request group, 3) mark pages RO in platform VM so kernels assert. Pseudocode for hint usage in runtime config: 
```
kernel_hint: {
  "dequant_strategy": "INLINE_DEQUANT",   // INLINE_DEQUANT | COPY_DEQUANT | NO_DEQUANT
  "kv_aliasable": true,
  "alignment": 64
}
```
We should also expose a per-model override for models that are sensitive to quantization rounding.

maria: Good — validation at kernel load time sounds right. Can you sketch what the validation should check? Example: ensure kernel does not call any Write op for KV pointers, and assert alignment >= declared alignment.

jonah: Load-time checks: 1) static code scan for write paths to kernel KV API (fast), 2) runtime smoke that runs a small batch through the kernel in a sandbox and checks page permissions remain RO. If either fails, mark kernel as COPY_DEQUANT-only. Also we should add an attribute to kernel registry: `requires_copy_on_kv` so scheduler can route.

elaine: From testing side — we'll need a reproducible harness to catch regressions from in-place dequant. Suggest tests: 
- unit/quant_kv_alias/alias_smoke.test (run in CI)
- perf/regression/quant_inline.p95 (collect p95 latency across a matrix)
- correctness/eval/quant_roundtrip.diff (compare logits to fp16 baseline within tolerance)
Run command: `./infra/test_harness/run.sh --suite=quant_kv_alias --iter=200 --model=gpt-medium`
Also add a chaos test where we forcibly change page protections mid-run to ensure kernels don't rely on writable pages.

kevin: Another operational detail — fallback policies for Dedicated vs Hosted: Hosted can fallback to COPY_DEQUANT transparently; Dedicated customers might prefer we error if their pinned kernel can't do INLINE_DEQUANT (so they detect missing optimization). Add config flag `runtime.experimental.quant_kv_alias = {mode: "canary"|"opt-in"|"strict"}`. Canary = server decides, opt-in = customer enables, strict = error on mismatch.

maria: Rollout plan proposal: 1) feature flag + load-time validation in dev cluster, 2) enable INLINE_DEQUANT for a quiet canary subset (5% traffic) with perf & correctness telemetry, 3) expand to 30% and run full evaluation suites, 4) GA with opt-in for Dedicated, strict for enterprise only after opt-in. We must gate GA on no correctness drifts beyond 1e-4 logit L2 on our eval set.

jonah: Perf counters to add: `quant.inline_tokens`, `quant.copy_tokens`, `quant.fallback_count`, `quant.kv_alias_hits`, and histograms for dequant latency. Also tag traces with `kernel_hint` so we can slice by strategy.

elaine: I'll add tests and perf collectors. For the eval tolerance, let's be explicit: compare logits after dequant/inference to fp16 baseline, require max-abs-diff < 1e-3 for int8, < 3e-3 for int4, and for fp8 use model-specific thresholds. We'll log diffs to S3 and fail CI if diffs spike.

kevin: One last gotcha — mixed-precision KV where K uses int4 and V uses int8 is a real use-case. Our hint should be per-tensor, not global. So update API to accept per-kv-slot strategy, e.g., `kv_strategies: [{k: INLINE_DEQUANT, v: COPY_DEQUANT}, ...]`. That complicates allocator guarantees but doable.

maria: Good call. I'll update the RFC with: 1) kernel hint API (per-tensor), 2) aliasing contract + load-time validation, 3) rollout plan + feature flag semantics, 4) test matrix and perf counters.

sre-bot: deploybot: Canary rollout (runtime-experimental/quant_kv_alias=canary) triggered on cluster dev-3 at 2024-06-19T15:00Z by maria. Monitor: dashboards/quant_kv_alias.

jonah: Thanks — can we also add a small safety net: if the inline path's dequant produces a high-entropy spike (sudden token distribution change), the router auto-fails to COPY_DEQUANT for that request id. Basically runtime-level correctness circuit breaker.

maria: Yes — add `correctness_circuit_breaker` that compares ngram logits on a small sample and flags. We'll add to rollout checklist. I'll open a follow-up with the updated RFC patch and include the validation script.

jonah: Sounds good. I'm going to sketch the kernel registry changes and open a PR.

kevin: I'll start the allocator changes and add the page-protection helpers.

elaine: Tests/CI PR incoming from me tomorrow.

maria: Great teamwork — thanks all. We'll aim to land the RFC changes by end of sprint. :rocket:
